newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russia tax chief tenders resignation.
newsitem.headline: Russia tax chief tenders resignation.

text.p: The head of Russia's State Tax Service, Vitaly Artyukhov, has tendered his resignation to Prime Minister Viktor Chernomyrdin, a spokeswoman for the agency told Reuters on Monday in confirmation of earlier media reports.

Chernomyrdin had yet to accept the resignation and the two men would meet on Tuesday, she said. She could not say what had motivated Artyukhov's decision but said the staff of the tax service did not want him to leave.

The prime minister said at the weekend that he expected to make more personnel changes in the administration following a sweeping cabinet reshuffle last month that brought in more liberal reformers committed to increasing tax revenues.
The government blames massive tax evasion for depriving it of funds to pay state workers, pensioners and welfare claimants.
Deputy Prime Minister Alfred Kokh said at the weekend that tax collection in the first quarter was only 58 percent of that budgeted for. He called it "a crisis of statehood".
The 20 biggest non-payers of tax account for about 60 percent of the debts owed by the government, Kokh added.
